dedupe_keys.name: gslp matlab gnss satellite look angle predictor for multi constellation visibility simulation

description: GSLP, the GNSS Satellite Look Angle Predictor, is a Matlab-based utility that predicts GNSS satellite look angles and simulates satellite trajectories from any point over any time span. The paper says it addresses shortcomings of existing tools, uses NORAD two-line element files as input, shows results visually and writes ASCII files, supports GPS, GLONASS, Galileo and NavIC (IRNSS), and can be used for real-time mission planning and GNSS research; it motivates the tool by the roughly 100 GNSS satellites now visible from any location. Producer: Sukabya Dan, Atanu Santra, Somnath Mahato, Partha Rakshit and Anindya Bose, published on 17 November 2019. Coverage: worldwide, for any observation point. Access: the publisher page was blocked, so the abstract came from the OpenAlex record; no download location for the software was found, so open_source is recorded as false, meaning no verified open-source release. Licence and cost: not stated. Caveats: it needs Matlab and a distribution route was not confirmed. Simulation uses: it supports positioning availability planning and satellite visibility studies. Related record: the G-CAT GNSS coverage analysis tool (model-g-cat-gnss-coverage-analysis-tool).
